q: Batteries and generators are called sources of _____ force.
e: Batteries and generators are called sources of electromotive force. Put magnetomotive or gravitational in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: A battery converts _____ energy into electrical energy to provide electrical power.
e: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy to provide electrical power. Put mechanical or nuclear in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: In an electric generator, _____ energy is converted into electrical energy.
e: In an electric generator, mechanical energy is converted into electrical energy. Put chemical or heat in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field.

q: The main function of the source is to send negative charges from the positive terminal to the _____ terminal within the source.
e: The main function of the source is to send negative charges from the positive terminal to the negative terminal within the source. Put earth or neutral in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. From the positive terminal to the _____ terminal within the source. negative.

q: Electromotive force is the amount of energy provided by the battery per unit charge to move round the _____ circuit.
e: Electromotive force is the amount of energy provided by the battery per unit charge to move round the complete circuit. open is not complete, and parallel is not complete either. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: The unit of electromotive force is volt, equivalent to _____ per coulomb of electric charge.
e: The unit of electromotive force is volt, equivalent to joule per coulomb of electric charge. Put watt or ampere in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: Despite its name, electromotive force is not actually a _____.
e: Despite its name, electromotive force is not actually a force. energy is not force, and power is not force either. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: The internal resistance of a battery depends on its size, chemical properties, life time, and _____.
e: The internal resistance of a battery depends on its size, chemical properties, life time, and temperature. Put voltage or current in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Terminal voltage is emf minus Ir, so it sags when the load current rises.

q: A battery which has an internal resistance $r$ must be viewed as having a resistor of resistance $r$ connected in _____ to the battery.
e: A battery which has an internal resistance r must be viewed as having a resistor of resistance r connected in series to the battery. parallel is not series, and opposition is not series either. Terminal voltage is emf minus Ir, so it sags when the load current rises. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: The equation $E = IR + Ir$ is called the _____ equation.
e: The equation E = IR + Ir is called the circuit equation. Put loop or junction in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. The relation in this line is E = IR + Ir is called the _____ equation.

q: The potential difference across the terminals of a battery connected to an external circuit is called the _____ voltage.
e: The potential difference across the terminals of a battery connected to an external circuit is called the terminal voltage. Put open or internal in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

q: Electromotive force (emf) is the potential difference between the two terminals of a battery in an _____ circuit.
e: Electromotive force (emf) is the potential difference between the two terminals of a battery in an open circuit. Put closed or parallel in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: Terminal voltage is the potential difference between the two terminals of a battery in a _____ circuit.
e: Terminal voltage is the potential difference between the two terminals of a battery in a closed circuit. Put open or series in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: When a battery having an internal resistance is used in an electric circuit, the potential difference between the terminals is always _____ than its emf.
e: When a battery having an internal resistance is used in an electric circuit, the potential difference between the terminals is always less than its emf. Put greater or equal in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: When charging a battery, the potential difference between the terminals is equal to _____.
e: When charging a battery, the potential difference between the terminals is equal to E + Ir. Put E - Ir or E in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: The potential difference or voltage is the amount of energy required to move a unit charge from one end to another end of a circuit _____.
e: The potential difference or voltage is the amount of energy required to move a unit charge from one end to another end of a circuit element. source is not element, and node is not element either. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current.

q: In charging a battery, the chemical energy which has been used up is supplied back by _____ energy from some external source.
e: In charging a battery, the chemical energy which has been used up is supplied back by electrical energy from some external source. mechanical is not electrical, and heat is not electrical either. While charging, plate voltage climbs toward the battery value as 1 minus a decaying exponential. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: A steady current will flow through the conductor if a steady _____ difference is maintained between its ends.
e: A steady current will flow through the conductor if a steady potential difference is maintained between its ends. Put kinetic or thermal in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: The positive charges are sent from the negative terminal to the _____ terminal within the source.
e: The positive charges are sent from the negative terminal to the neutral terminal within the source. Put earth or positive in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. From the negative terminal to the _____ terminal within the source. neutral.

q: By Ohm's law, the potential difference across the resistor is $V =$ _____.
e: By Ohm's law, the potential difference across the resistor is V = IR. I/R is not IR, and R/I is not IR either. Ohm's law is V = IR for ohmic parts at constant temperature.

q: The total work done in moving a unit positive charge round the complete circuit is _____, which is the emf $E$ of the battery.
e: The total work done in moving a unit positive charge round the complete circuit is IR+Ir, which is the emf E of the battery. Put IR-Ir or I(R-r) in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: The internal resistance of a battery is represented by the symbol _____.
e: The internal resistance of a battery is represented by the symbol r. Put R or E in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat.

q: The emf of a battery is represented by the symbol _____.
e: The emf of a battery is represented by the symbol E. Put V or I in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: The work done in moving a unit positive charge from one end to another of the internal resistance $r$ of the battery is _____.
e: The work done in moving a unit positive charge from one end to another of the internal resistance r of the battery is Ir. Put IR or I^2r in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: In an open circuit, the terminal voltage $V$ is related to emf $E$ by the equation $V =$ _____.
e: In an open circuit, the terminal voltage V is related to emf E by the equation V = E. Put E-Ir or E+Ir in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Terminal voltage is emf minus Ir, so it sags when the load current rises.

q: When a battery is charging, the terminal voltage $V$ is _____ than its emf $E$.
e: When a battery is charging, the terminal voltage V is greater than its emf E. less is not greater, and equal is not greater either. Terminal voltage is emf minus Ir, so it sags when the load current rises.

q: When two or more electromotive sources are connected in series, the resultant emf is the _____ sum of the individual emfs.
e: When two or more electromotive sources are connected in series, the resultant emf is the algebraic sum of the individual emfs. geometric is not algebraic, and arithmetic is not algebraic either. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

q: In a series aiding arrangement, the currents leaving the batteries are in the _____ direction.
e: In a series aiding arrangement, the currents leaving the batteries are in the same direction. Put opposite or perpendicular in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: In series opposing, the resultant emf is the _____ between the individual emfs.
e: In series opposing, the resultant emf is the difference between the individual emfs. Put sum or product in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

q: In a series connection of batteries, the total internal resistance is the _____ of the individual internal resistances.
e: In a series connection of batteries, the total internal resistance is the sum of the individual internal resistances. Put difference or product in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

q: In parallel connection of batteries, care must be taken that the terminal of the same _____ should be connected together.
e: In parallel connection of batteries, care must be taken that the terminal of the same polarity should be connected together. magnitude is not polarity, and resistance is not polarity either. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: If batteries in parallel are not connected with the same polarity together, batteries may be _____.
e: If batteries in parallel are not connected with the same polarity together, batteries may be damaged. Put charged or cooled in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add.

q: For two batteries with equal emfs $E$ and equal internal resistances $r$ connected in parallel, the resultant emf is _____.
e: For two batteries with equal emfs E and equal internal resistances r connected in parallel, the resultant emf is E. Put 2E or E/2 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. Terminal voltage is emf minus Ir, so it sags when the load current rises.

q: For two batteries with equal internal resistances $r$ connected in parallel, the resultant internal resistance is _____.
e: For two batteries with equal internal resistances r connected in parallel, the resultant internal resistance is r/2. 2r is not r/2, and r is not r/2 either. Terminal voltage is emf minus Ir, so it sags when the load current rises. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: In a series aiding arrangement, the batteries can be regarded as a single battery having an emf of _____.
e: In a series aiding arrangement, the batteries can be regarded as a single battery having an emf of E1 + E2. E1 - E2 is not E1 + E2, and E1 × E2 is not E1 + E2 either. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

q: In series opposing, the total internal resistance of the two batteries is _____.
e: In series opposing, the total internal resistance of the two batteries is r1 + r2. Put r1 - r2 or r1 / r2 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Terminal voltage is emf minus Ir, so it sags when the load current rises.

q: In parallel connection of batteries, the resultant emf of the parallel-combination is just the emf $E$ of a _____ battery.
e: In parallel connection of batteries, the resultant emf of the parallel-combination is just the emf E of a single battery. Put double or triple in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: Electrical energy is energy associated with the flow of _____ through any part of circuit.
e: Electrical energy is energy associated with the flow of charge through any part of circuit. mass is not charge, and heat is not charge either. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: Electrical energy can be generated from sources of emf such as batteries, generators, dynamos and _____ cells.
e: Electrical energy can be generated from sources of emf such as batteries, generators, dynamos and photovoltaic cells. fuel is not photovoltaic, and primary is not photovoltaic either. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

e: Electrical energy can be stored in fuel cells, batteries, capacitors and inductors. resistors and transformers belong to other processes, not this inductors case. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: The work done by the battery in taking the charge $Q$ from A to B is transformed into _____ energy in the resistor.
e: The work done by the battery in taking the charge Q from A to B is transformed into heat energy in the resistor. light is not heat, and mechanical is not heat either. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: Heat energy is produced in a resistor because _____ collide with the atoms in the resistor when they pass through it.
e: Heat energy is produced in a resistor because electrons collide with the atoms in the resistor when they pass through it. protons is not electrons, and neutrons is not electrons either. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow.

q: The practical unit of electrical energy is _____ hour.
e: The practical unit of electrical energy is kilowatt hour. Put volt or ampere in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: $1 \text{ kWh}$ is equal to $1000 \text{ W} \times 1 \text{ h}$, which is _____ J.
e: 1 kWh is equal to 1000 W × 1 h, which is 3. 60 × 10^6 J. Put 3. 60 × 10^3 or 3.

q: Electrical power is the _____ of transfer of electrical energy.
e: Electrical power is the rate of transfer of electrical energy. amount is not rate, and capacity is not rate either. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: If 1 joule of electrical energy is transferred in 1 second, the electrical power is 1 _____.
e: If 1 joule of electrical energy is transferred in 1 second, the electrical power is 1 watt. volt is not watt, and joule is not watt either. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: The unit of electrical power is watt, which is equivalent to _____ per second.
e: The unit of electrical power is watt, which is equivalent to joule per second. Put ampere or volt in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R.

q: If an electric motor is connected to a battery, the electrical energy will be transformed into _____ energy.

q: The electrical energy $W$ produced by the battery is equal to $VIt$, $I^2Rt$, or _____.
e: The electrical energy W produced by the battery is equal to VIt, I^2Rt, or (V^2)/(R)t. Put V^2 R t or V I / t in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: The unit of electrical energy kWh stands for _____ hour.
e: The unit of electrical energy kWh stands for kilowatt hour. kilovolt is not kilowatt, and kiloampere is not kilowatt either. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: When electric current passes through a conductor, the electrons are accelerated due to electric _____.
e: When electric current passes through a conductor, the electrons are accelerated due to electric field. charge and potential belong to other processes, not this field case. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow.

q: Electrons lose their kinetic energy which appears as _____ energy.
e: Electrons lose their kinetic energy which appears as heat energy. potential is not heat, and mechanical is not heat either. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow.

q: The electrical energy $W$ is related to the amount of heat $H$ by the equation $W =$ _____.
e: The electrical energy W is related to the amount of heat H by the equation W = JH. J/H is not JH, and H/J is not JH either. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: In the equation $W = JH$, $J$ is a constant called Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat, which has a value of _____ $\text{J cal}^{-1}$.
e: In the equation W = JH, J is a constant called Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat, which has a value of 4. 2 J cal^-1. Put 4. 8 or 3.

q: Joule's law states that the amount of heat produced is directly proportional to the _____ of the current.
e: Joule's law states that the amount of heat produced is directly proportional to the square of the current. Put inverse or cube in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: According to Joule's law, heat produced is directly proportional to the value of resistance and the _____ taken by the current.
e: According to Joule's law, heat produced is directly proportional to the value of resistance and the time taken by the current. distance and voltage belong to other processes, not this time case. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat. Joule heat is I^2 R t; it grows with current squared.

q: The formula for heat $H$ produced in a resistor in calories is $H =$ _____.
e: The formula for heat H produced in a resistor in calories is H = (I^2Rt)/(J). Put I^2Rt × J or IRt/J in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat.

q: The formula for heat $H$ using voltage $V$ is $H = \frac{V^2 t}{R \times}$ _____.
e: The formula for heat H using voltage V is H = (V^2 t)/(R ×) J. I is not J, and W is not J either. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

q: English physicist James Prescott Joule experimentally studied the heating effect of electric current in the year _____.
e: English physicist James Prescott Joule experimentally studied the heating effect of electric current in the year 1841. Put 1884 or 1941 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: In Joule's law, the constant $J$ is called Joule's mechanical _____ of heat.
e: In Joule's law, the constant J is called Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat. Put capacity or efficiency in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Joule heat is I^2 R t; it grows with current squared.

q: Heat energy is produced in the resistor $R$ which acts as a heating _____.
e: Heat energy is produced in the resistor R which acts as a heating coil. capacitor is not coil, and inductor is not coil either. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat.

q: The formula for heat $H$ using voltage $V$ and current $I$ is $H =$ _____.
e: The formula for heat H using voltage V and current I is H = (VIt)/(J). VIt × J is not (VIt)/(J), and (VI)/(Jt) is not (VIt)/(J) either. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: The heating effect of electric current has special applications in _____ appliances.
e: The heating effect of electric current has special applications in domestic appliances. Put industrial or medical in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: An electric light bulb consists of a glass bulb containing a _____ filament.

q: The tungsten filament has a high melting point of approximately _____ $^\circ\text{C}$.
e: The tungsten filament has a high melting point of approximately 3000 ^°C. 1800 is not 3000, and 2500 is not 3000 either. The bulb filament is tungsten because it can sit near 3000 °C without melting.

q: Because of the inert gas, the light bulb can be used safely up to the temperature _____ $^\circ\text{C}$.

e: An electric iron typically has an electric power of 750 - 1000 W. Put 500 or 2000 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. An electric iron typically has an electric power of 750 - _____ W. 1000.

q: A 13 A fuse should be fitted for appliances rated above _____ W.
e: A 13 A fuse should be fitted for appliances rated above 700 W. 500 is not 700, and 1000 is not 700 either. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose.

q: In a circuit with a 3 A fuse and 220 V source, the maximum power which can safely be consumed is _____ W.
e: In a circuit with a 3 A fuse and 220 V source, the maximum power which can safely be consumed is 660 W. 330 is not 660, and 220 is not 660 either. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose.

q: The electrical energy consumed by an air conditioner drawing 10 A from a 220 V line is calculated using the formula $P =$ _____.
e: The electrical energy consumed by an air conditioner drawing 10 A from a 220 V line is calculated using the formula P = VI. Put V/I or I/V in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.
